abstract: This paper presents a framework for steering technological progress to increase labor demand and mitigate displacement effects. The authors argue that actively guiding innovation becomes increasingly desirable as social safety nets become less efficient, suggesting policy intervention in technological development as a complement or alternative to income support mechanisms.
keyFindings: Technological progress can be steered through policy to increase labor demand rather than reduce it
The desirability of steering technology is inversely related to the efficiency of social safety nets
Policy intervention in innovation direction serves as an alternative approach to addressing technological displacement
